questions.prompt: Let S = (0, 1). Which statements are true?
questions.explanation: S has no endpoints in it, so it has no max or min, but its sup and inf are 1 and 0.

questions.prompt: The ordered field ℚ satisfies the Completeness Axiom.
questions.explanation: The set {q ∈ ℚ : q² < 2} is bounded above in ℚ but has no least upper bound in ℚ.

questions.prompt: Name the property stating that for every real x there is a natural number n with n > x.
questions.explanation: This follows from the Completeness Axiom.

questions.prompt: For the sequence a_n = 1/n converging to 0, what is the smallest N such that |a_n| < 0.01 for all n ≥ N?
questions.explanation: 1/n < 0.01 iff n > 100, so the first valid n is 101.

questions.prompt: Every convergent sequence of real numbers is bounded.
questions.explanation: Past some N the terms lie within 1 of the limit, and only finitely many terms remain.

questions.prompt: Explain why every Cauchy sequence of real numbers converges.
rubric: Shows a Cauchy sequence is bounded
Applies Bolzano-Weierstrass to get a convergent subsequence
Shows the whole sequence converges to the same limit using the Cauchy condition (ε/2 argument)
questions.model: A Cauchy sequence is bounded, so by Bolzano-Weierstrass it has a subsequence converging to some L. Given ε, pick N with |a_m − a_n| < ε/2 for m, n ≥ N and a subsequence term a_{n_k} with |a_{n_k} − L| < ε/2 and n_k ≥ N. Then |a_n − L| < ε for all n ≥ N.
questions.explanation: Boundedness plus a convergent subsequence plus the Cauchy condition forces convergence.

questions.prompt: Which subset of ℝ is compact?
questions.explanation: By Heine-Borel, a subset of ℝ is compact iff closed and bounded.

questions.prompt: Match each set to its description.
questions.explanation: Check each endpoint and whether every point has a neighborhood inside the set.

questions.prompt: The only subsets of ℝ that are both open and closed are ∅ and ℝ.
questions.explanation: This is equivalent to ℝ being connected.

questions.prompt: Name the theorem guaranteeing that a continuous function on [a, b] attains a maximum and a minimum.
questions.explanation: Compactness of [a, b] gives attained extrema.

questions.prompt: The function f(x) = 1/x is uniformly continuous on (0, 1).
questions.explanation: Near 0 the same δ cannot work for every point; for fixed ε the required δ shrinks to 0.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of an ε-δ proof that f is continuous at c in order.
items: Choose δ in terms of ε
questions.explanation: The proof fixes ε first, then picks δ, then verifies the conclusion.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = x² on [0, 2], the Mean Value Theorem gives a point c with f′(c) = (f(2) − f(0))/(2 − 0). What is c?
questions.explanation: The average slope is 4/2 = 2, and f′(c) = 2c = 2 gives c = 1.

questions.prompt: The function f(x) = |x| is continuous at 0 but not differentiable at 0.
questions.explanation: The one-sided derivatives are −1 and 1, so the limit of the difference quotient does not exist.

questions.prompt: Use the Mean Value Theorem to show that if f′(x) = 0 for all x in an interval, then f is constant on that interval.
rubric: Takes two arbitrary points a < b in the interval
Applies MVT to get c with f(b) − f(a) = f′(c)(b − a)
questions.model: Take any a < b in the interval. By MVT there is c in (a, b) with f(b) − f(a) = f′(c)(b − a) = 0, so f(a) = f(b). Since a and b were arbitrary, f is constant.
questions.explanation: MVT converts a zero derivative into equal function values.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = x on [0, 1] with a uniform partition into 4 subintervals, what is the upper sum U(f, P)?
questions.explanation: f is increasing so the sup on each piece is the right endpoint: (1/4)(1/4+2/4+3/4+1) = 10/16 = 0.625.

questions.prompt: If f is continuous on [a, b] and F(x) = ∫ₐˣ f(t) dt, what does the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus say about F?
choices: F′(x) = f(x) for all x in [a, b]
F′(x) = f(x) only where f is differentiable
questions.answer: F′(x) = f(x) for all x in [a, b]
questions.explanation: Part 1 of the FTC says the accumulation function is an antiderivative of continuous f.

questions.prompt: Every bounded function on [a, b] is Riemann integrable.
questions.explanation: The Dirichlet function (1 on rationals, 0 on irrationals) is bounded but has upper sum 1 and lower sum 0 for every partition.
